exchanges.a: I am a Christian. I was baptized in 2014 at the {CHURCH} church.

exchanges.q: What was your role in the church?
exchanges.a: I taught the Bible to children on Sundays, and I helped Pastor {PASTOR} with the meetings in people's homes.

a: During a Sunday service, men from the {GROUP} came into the church.
They took the pastor and three young men. We never saw the pastor again.

exchanges.a: Yes, I was there. I hid in the back room with the children.

exchanges.q: What happened to you after that?
exchanges.a: Two weeks later they detained me at my workplace. They kept me for nine days and asked me for the names of the other members.

exchanges.q: Were you ever charged with a crime?
exchanges.a: No, they never charged me. They released me when I signed a paper that I could not read.
I don't know exactly. I think it said that I would stop going to the church.

exchanges.q: Did you continue to practice your religion after your release?
exchanges.a: Yes, but only in secret, in my house, with my wife and my mother.

exchanges.q: When did you arrive in the United States?
exchanges.a: I arrived on the twentieth of July 2020. I asked for asylum at the border.
